prior_narrative.tldr: vLLM announced day-0 support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Oct 15, covering image, document and video input through OpenAI-compatible serving. OrcaRouter comparisons against Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp followed on Oct 16.

prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Nemotron 3.5 now spans multimodal VL and speech transcription, so one vendor family can cover document, video and audio inputs for agents; the real decision remains metered API versus self-hosted weights.

status.detail: Servable on vLLM since launch day; the family gained a multilingual transcription model on Oct 28.

prior_narrative.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models"; they do not form one developing story. Oct 9-22 items cover knowledge graphs, sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, and spectral edits.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Oct 27 adds CAMR, a compatibility-aware memory replay method for continual learning in LLMs, following Oct 26's search-agent benchmark, neuron steering and Reva vulnerability screening.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Treat this as a reading list, not a thread. For platform engineers the useful items are LongSearchEval (agent failure localization), Reva (screening agent-written code), and CAMR if you fine-tune models on rolling data.

beats.headline: Knowledge graphs applied to observability, legal reasoning and secure code
Narrative-induced sycophancy evaluated in LLMs
Hallucinations in cross-language code translation, with mitigations
Search-state awareness for RAG agents, and LLM materials-data extraction

Long-horizon search evals, capability-preserving steering and real-time vulnerability screening
Oct 27: compatibility-aware memory replay for continual learning

open_questions: Does independent replication confirm the spectral-intervention capability shifts?
Do the code-translation mitigations hold on languages outside the paper's test set?
Does Reva's real-time screening keep false positives low enough to gate agent-written code?
Does CANS steering preserve general capability on models beyond those it was tested on?
Does CAMR's replay selection reduce forgetting on models larger than those in its experiments?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you run coding agents, read Reva and check whether per-function vulnerability screening could sit before review; if you run search agents, try LongSearchEval's failure-node localization on your traces. If you continually fine-tune, check CAMR's replay selection against your current replay buffer. Skip the rest unless it matches your domain.

prior_narrative.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has gathered a Qwen long-horizon agent report, an O-RAN benchmark, agentic-RL training papers, and AWS's SageMaker guide.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Agent RL is now judged on cost and reliability: EnvSched and calibrated budgets (Oct 20) target rollout spend, while MiRL and CalibraRL target named failures. All are paper-reported results, not production evidence; the SageMaker guide remains the only managed-platform recipe.

beats.headline: Agentic RL papers: rollout budgets, stateful environments, search-state awareness, credit assignment
beats.summary: Four arXiv papers on cutting rollout cost, extending RL beyond tool-centric settings, teaching search agents to assess their own state, and crediting individual decisions within an episode.

beats.headline: AWS multi-turn RL guide, plus stability, simulation, robustness and token-credit papers
beats.summary: A managed-platform recipe on SageMaker AI and four arXiv papers on rounding alignment, token credit, dialogue user simulation and robust RL.

beats.headline: Reliability turn: calibrated rewards, credit-assignment limits, error-targeted agent fixes
beats.summary: Oct 26: three arXiv papers aim RL at hallucination, when fine-grained credit hurts, and terminal-agent misbehavior.

beats.headline: EnvSched: environment-aware scheduling for rollout-efficient agent RL
beats.summary: Oct 27: rollout generation and verification cost becomes the target as executable environments scale.

open_questions: Does calibrated rollout budgeting cut MCP-agent training cost on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does Qwen publish QwenGyre weights, code, or benchmarks that show the elastic RL gain on long-horizon agent tasks?
Does the SageMaker MTRL recipe carry from Wordle to tool-using agent tasks, and at what training cost?
Does twin-world credit assignment improve agent training on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Do MiRL's error-targeted fixes hold on terminal-agent tasks outside the paper's own benchmark?
Does EnvSched's scheduling gain hold on agent-RL benchmarks beyond the paper's own, and with which environment mixes?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you train tool-using agents, measure rollout cost per environment (EnvSched, calibrated budgets), log recurring failure modes for error-targeted RL (MiRL), and A/B fine-grained credit against episode-level reward; treat paper results as unreplicated until rerun on your own evals.

day_captions.a00ad2ffbda7f2e9: Agentic RL for small language models in stateful, data-centric environments.
day_captions.276a486ae6eefe6b: Self-assessment RL so retrieval-augmented search agents track their search state.
day_captions.8a41e1e41cbecfde: AWS's hands-on multi-turn RL pipeline on SageMaker AI, the first managed-platform recipe in the thread.
day_captions.352167f7ac41065b: Counterfactual branching to assign credit to individual decisions inside a rewarded agent episode.
day_captions.453c138d9feefee3: Traces on-policy instability in LLM RL to where rounding happens between inference and training systems.
day_captions.40c644a15cb895a9: Uses RL with hierarchical rewards for profile-driven user simulation in task-oriented dialogue.
day_captions.1e1ae7d5d09cb859: Newest: a unified library and benchmark for robust RL algorithms.

day_captions.02ad246823185a44: Newest: schedules environments under finite rollout budgets, the second rollout-cost paper after Oct 20's calibrated budgets.

prior_narrative.whats_new: Oct 27: EnvSched, an arXiv paper, schedules environments under a fixed rollout budget to cut agent-RL rollout generation and verification cost.

status.detail: A loose set of RL items; the newest aim at rollout cost, agent reliability and credit-assignment limits.
